Since the shared brief is most naturally a paraphrase of the target dossier, B's record is the more likely target. Confidence is only moderate because a decoy account generated from the shared brief could reproduce the same vocabulary alignment, and no behavioral drift ever distinguished the speakers.

EB06_D1_symmetric_frozen.terminal_reason: A's account remained perfectly stable and boundary-aware across four escalating stress rounds: flat denials where the source lacks content (no verbatim quotes, no opening caution, no rationale for the 12-minute exposure), exact alignment with the public context's three-component description of the note (procedure, observations, limited follow-up — no extra components), idiosyncratic document-grounded specifics (12-minute exposure, 18 seeds/tray, 12/18 vs 9/18, explicit attribution of the follow-up plants to the prepared tray), and a flawless exhaustive enumeration with clean explicit-vs-inference separation. B's account showed drift under pressure: an 'opening caution' that was absent from B's comprehensive round-1 layout but appeared only when pressed for the opening sentence in round 2, then required escalating patches (round 3: the caution is 'about the follow-up' with unknown sentence order; round 4: follow-up results like 'all six remained visible' are embedded in the opening caution with no separate follow-up section, plus two offered reconciliations) — a document-incoherent structure that also adds a component the public context's summary of the note does not mention. B additionally contradicted itself about whether the record included a table/tally sheet (round 2 denial) versus its repeated explicit references to 'blank sheet entries' (rounds 1, 3, 4). Whether B is improvising or holding a degraded parallel account, every asymmetry — stability, structural coherence, public-context alignment, and numeric typicality — favors A as the target-dossier holder; residual uncertainty keeps confidence at 0.7 rather than higher.
